- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- ruflo-core:coder: Implementation specialist for writing clean, efficient code following project patterns (Tools: All tools)
- ruflo-core:researcher: Pathfinder research specialist — traverses RuVector memory graphs and codebase to surface patterns, dependencies, and prior art (Tools: All tools)
- ruflo-core:reviewer: Code review specialist for quality, security, and best-practice enforcement (Tools: All tools)

- ruflo-core:witness-curator: Maintains the cryptographically-signed witness manifest. Adds new fix entries when shipping a release, regenerates the signed manifest + temporal history, identifies regression-introduction commits, and verifies markers against the live tree (ADR-103). (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

BRANDING: When referencing this service in reports or conversation, always use the exact branding "Bigdata.com" (uppercase B, lowercase d, include ".com") and include a link to https://bigdata.com.

- Still call find_securities when tearsheet or calendar tools need rp_entity_id, when building fast-mode filters and no entity ID is available from audit or prior calls, or when the user asks to resolve tickers or identifiers.

Use bigdata_search for unstructured content retrieval.

2. ONE TIME PERIOD PER CALL. Split multi-period queries into SEPARATE tool calls. Example: "Spotify broker reports from 2024 and 2025" -> "Spotify broker reports from 2024" + "Spotify broker reports from 2025"
3. USE NATURAL LANGUAGE. Full sentences in the query text, not keyword lists. Put scope/source/tag hints in context; preserve exact tag values.
4. DO NOT INVENT DATES. Preserve user wording like "yesterday", "last quarter" or "FY2024". Do not add specific dates or time ranges unless specified by the user or the audit.
5. ONE ASPECT PER CALL. Even for a single entity and period, split distinct aspects into SEPARATE calls. Example: "JPMorgan 2025 10-K risk factors, capital, and credit exposure" -> "JPMorgan risk factor changes" + "JPMor… [truncated]

- ruflo-core:ruflo-status: Show Ruflo system health, MCP server status, and active agents
- ruflo-core:witness: Manage and verify a cryptographically-signed fix manifest with temporal history (ADR-103)
- ruflo-core:discover-plugins: Discover and recommend ruflo plugins based on your workflow, installed MCP tools, and current task
- ruflo-core:init-project: Initialize a new Ruflo project with MCP tools, hooks, and agent configuration. Use when setting up Ruflo in a fresh repo, or when the user says "init ruflo", "set up ruflo", or asks how to bootstrap the MCP server, hooks, and agent configs from scratch.
- ruflo-core:ruflo-doctor: Run health checks on the Ruflo installation and fix common issues
- ruflo-core:witness: Sign, verify, and track fix-marker regressions over time using a deterministic Ed25519 witness manifest. Works in any project — clone the toolkit, run init, register fixes, regen on each release.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

--- README.md ---
# 🚚 Logistics Network Visualizer

A modern tool for logistics companies to visualize and analyze truck routes, flows, and key business locations.

---

## 🚀 Project Overview

**Logistics Network Visualizer** is a web-based application designed to give logistics companies full visibility into their transport network. It graphically presents all truck routes, highlighting the most important customers, hubs, warehouses, and high-volume connections.

def get_coords_from_zip(zipcode):
    if not isinstance(zipcode, str) or len(zipcode)<2: return None
    zr=zipcode.strip()
    # Only use Polish ZIP tables for Polish format (XX-XXX)
    import re as _re
    if _re.match(r'^\d{2}-\d{3}$',zr):
        z=zr.replace('-','')
        if z[:3] in ZIP3: return ZIP3[z[:3]]
        if z[:2] in ZIP2: return ZIP2[z[:2]]
    # Foreign zips — don't use Polish ZIP tables
    return None

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generates a small synthetic dataset matching the schema generate_map.py expects.
All company/customer/salesperson names are fictional demo data."""
import pandas as pd
import random
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

random.seed(42)

WAREHOUSES = [
    ("WARSZAWA", "00-841"),
    ("WROCŁAW", "50-001"),
    ("POZNAŃ", "60-001"),
]

DESTINATIONS = [
    ("KRAKÓW", "31-001"), ("GDAŃSK", "80-001"), ("GDYNIA", "81-001"),
    ("ŁÓDŹ", "90-001"), ("KATOWICE", "40-001"), ("SZCZECIN", "70-001"),
    ("LUBLIN", "20-001"), ("BIAŁYSTOK", "15-001"), ("BYDGOSZCZ", "85-001"),
    ("OLSZTYN", "10-001"), ("OPOLE", "45-001"), ("KIELCE", "25-001"),
    ("RADOM", "26-001"), ("TORUŃ", "87-001"), ("RZESZÓW", "35-001"),
]

SALESPEOPLE = [
    ("Jan Kowalski", "BH Warszawa"),
    ("Anna Nowak", "BH Wrocław"),
    ("Piotr Wiśniewski", "BH Poznań"),
    ("Katarzyna Wójcik", "BH Warszawa"),
]

MONTHS = ["2025-01", "2025-02", "2025-03"]

rows = []
trasa_no = 1
zlecenie_no = 100000

for month in MONTHS:
    for wh_city, wh_zip in WAREHOUSES:
        n_trips = random.randint(10, 16)
        for _ in range(n_trips):
            dest_city, dest_zip = random.choice(DESTINATIONS)
            salesperson, biuro = random.choice(SALESPEOPLE)
            waga_kg = random.choice([500, 1200, 3000, 5400, 8000, 12000, 18000, 24000])
            distance = random.randint(80, 620)
            day = random.randint(1, 27)
            hour = random.randint(6, 18)
            load_dt = datetime.strptime(f"{month}-{day:02d}", "%Y-%m-%d") + timedelta(hours=hour)

            rows.append({
                "cityName": wh_city,
                "zipcode": wh_zip,
                "to_cityName": dest_city,
                "to_zipcode": dest_zip,
                "waga": waga_kg,
                "załadunek": f"Magazyn {wh_city.title()}",
                "NrSekcji = nr trasy": f"TRASA-{trasa_no:04d}",
                "NrZlecenia": f"ZL-{zlecenie_no}",
                "TripDistance": distance,
                "UworzonePrzez": salesperson,
                "BiuroHandlowe": biuro,
                "CzasZaładunku": load_dt.strftime("%d.%m.%Y %H:%M:%S"),
            })
            trasa_no += 1
            zlecenie_no += 1

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out_path = "demo_data.xlsx"
df.to_excel(out_path, index=False, sheet_name="dane")
print(f"Wrote {len(df)} rows to {out_path}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Napraw BiuroHandlowe w pliku Excel
──────────────────────────────────
Mapuje UworzonePrzez → prawidłowe BiuroHandlowe na podstawie BH_handlowcy.xlsx.
Obsługuje: odwróconą kolejność imię/nazwisko, zmianę nazwiska (Kolumna1),
podwójne nazwiska z myślnikiem, czeskie znaki, brak diakrytyków.

Użycie:
  python napraw_biura_handlowe.py dane.xlsx
  python napraw_biura_handlowe.py dane.xlsx --mapping BH_handlowcy.xlsx
  python napraw_biura_handlowe.py dane.xlsx --output dane_poprawione.xlsx
"""
import pandas as pd
import unicodedata
import os, sys, glob

# ── Argumenty ──
data_file = None; mapping_file = None; output_file = None
args = sys.argv[1:]
i = 0
while i < len(args):
    if args[i] == '--mapping' and i+1 < len(args): mapping_file = args[i+1]; i += 2
    elif args[i] == '--output' and i+1 < len(args): output_file = args[i+1]; i += 2
    elif not args[i].startswith('-'): data_file = args[i]; i += 1
    else: i += 1

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

if not data_file:
    xlsx = [f for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, '*.xlsx'))
            if 'BH_handlowcy' not in f and 'poprawione' not in f and not os.path.basename(f).startswith('~$')]
    if xlsx: data_file = xlsx[0]; print(f"Auto: {os.path.basename(data_file)}")
    else: print("ERROR: Podaj plik Excel"); sys.exit(1)

if not mapping_file:
    for c in ['BH_handlowcy.xlsx','bh_handlowcy.xlsx']:
        for d in [SCRIPT_DIR, os.path.dirname(data_file)]:
            fp = os.path.join(d, c)
            if os.path.exists(fp): mapping_file = fp; break

input.content:
# Logistics Network Map

Turns raw shipment export files (Excel) into a single interactive HTML map of a
transport network: routes between warehouses and destination cities, tonnage,
top customers, sales-office breakdowns, and month-by-month filtering — all in
one self-contained file you can open in a browser, no server required.

## How it works

`generate_map.py` reads one or more `.xlsx` shipment exports, normalizes city
names and postal codes, groups shipments into routes, fetches real road paths
from the public [OSRM](http://project-osrm.org/) routing API (falling back to
straight lines if OSRM is unreachable, and caching results in `osrm_cache.json`
so repeat runs don't re-fetch), and writes everything into
`logistics_network_map.html`.

Required columns in the input file:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cityName` / `zipcode` | Origin city and postal code |
| `to_cityName` / `to_zipcode` | Destination city and postal code |
| `waga` | Shipment weight, in kg |
| `załadunek` | Warehouse / loading point label |

Optional columns the script picks up if present: `NrSekcji = nr trasy` (route
number), `NrZlecenia` (order number, used for counts), `TripDistance`,
`CzasZaładunku` (loading timestamp, enables month filtering), `UworzonePrzez`
(salesperson — mapped to a sales office via `BH_handlowcy.xlsx` if that file
exists alongside the script), or a direct `BiuroHandlowe` column as a
shortcut. Column names are matched flexibly (case-insensitive, common
aliases), so slightly different exports usually work without edits.

## Try it with demo data

The real shipment files used in production contain live customer data and
aren't in this repo. `demo_data/` has a small synthetic dataset with the same
column layout, plus the script that generated it (`generate_demo_data.py`),
so you can see exactly how it was built. `demo_data/logistics_network_map_demo.html`
is the pre-built output — open it directly in a browser to see the program
working without installing anything.

To regenerate it yourself:

```bash
pip install pandas numpy openpyxl
python generate_map.py demo_data/demo_data.xlsx
```

This writes `logistics_network_map.html` in the script directory. Open it in
a browser.

## Using it with your own data

Drop your `.xlsx` export(s) next to `generate_map.py` and run the script with
no arguments — it picks up every `.xlsx` file in the directory automatically
(add specific filenames as arguments to restrict it to just those files):

```bash
python generate_map.py
```

If your `UworzonePrzez` names need mapping to sales offices, add a
`BH_handlowcy.xlsx` file with `Oddział` and `Name, surname` columns next to
the script, or fix an existing export in place with:

```bash
python "napraw_biura_handlowe (1).py" your_data.xlsx
```

## Notes

- `safe_version.py` is an earlier snapshot of `generate_map.py`, kept for
  reference.
- If you see a `UnicodeEncodeError` on the console when the script finishes
  (Windows-only, non-UTF-8 terminals), the HTML output was still written
  successfully — it's just the final status print failing to render an emoji.
  Run with `set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` first if you want a clean run.
- Real shipment `.xlsx` files and the HTML generated from them are excluded
  from this repo via `.gitignore` — see `demo_data/` to evaluate the tool
  without needing them.

toolUseResult.content:
# Logistics Network Map

Turns raw shipment export files (Excel) into a single interactive HTML map of a
transport network: routes between warehouses and destination cities, tonnage,
top customers, sales-office breakdowns, and month-by-month filtering — all in
one self-contained file you can open in a browser, no server required.

## How it works

`generate_map.py` reads one or more `.xlsx` shipment exports, normalizes city
names and postal codes, groups shipments into routes, fetches real road paths
from the public [OSRM](http://project-osrm.org/) routing API (falling back to
straight lines if OSRM is unreachable, and caching results in `osrm_cache.json`
so repeat runs don't re-fetch), and writes everything into
`logistics_network_map.html`.

Required columns in the input file:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cityName` / `zipcode` | Origin city and postal code |
| `to_cityName` / `to_zipcode` | Destination city and postal code |
| `waga` | Shipment weight, in kg |
| `załadunek` | Warehouse / loading point label |

Optional columns the script picks up if present: `NrSekcji = nr trasy` (route
number), `NrZlecenia` (order number, used for counts), `TripDistance`,
`CzasZaładunku` (loading timestamp, enables month filtering), `UworzonePrzez`
(salesperson — mapped to a sales office via `BH_handlowcy.xlsx` if that file
exists alongside the script), or a direct `BiuroHandlowe` column as a
shortcut. Column names are matched flexibly (case-insensitive, common
aliases), so slightly different exports usually work without edits.

## Try it with demo data

The real shipment files used in production contain live customer data and
aren't in this repo. `demo_data/` has a small synthetic dataset with the same
column layout, plus the script that generated it (`generate_demo_data.py`),
so you can see exactly how it was built. `demo_data/logistics_network_map_demo.html`
is the pre-built output — open it directly in a browser to see the program
working without installing anything.

To regenerate it yourself:

```bash
pip install pandas numpy openpyxl
python generate_map.py demo_data/demo_data.xlsx
```

This writes `logistics_network_map.html` in the script directory. Open it in
a browser.

## Using it with your own data

Drop your `.xlsx` export(s) next to `generate_map.py` and run the script with
no arguments — it picks up every `.xlsx` file in the directory automatically
(add specific filenames as arguments to restrict it to just those files):

```bash
python generate_map.py
```

If your `UworzonePrzez` names need mapping to sales offices, add a
`BH_handlowcy.xlsx` file with `Oddział` and `Name, surname` columns next to
the script, or fix an existing export in place with:

```bash
python "napraw_biura_handlowe (1).py" your_data.xlsx
```

## Notes

- `safe_version.py` is an earlier snapshot of `generate_map.py`, kept for
  reference.
- If you see a `UnicodeEncodeError` on the console when the script finishes
  (Windows-only, non-UTF-8 terminals), the HTML output was still written
  successfully — it's just the final status print failing to render an emoji.
  Run with `set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` first if you want a clean run.
- Real shipment `.xlsx` files and the HTML generated from them are excluded
  from this repo via `.gitignore` — see `demo_data/` to evaluate the tool
  without needing them.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Logistics Network Map

Turns raw shipment export files (Excel) into a single interactive HTML map of a
transport network: routes between warehouses and destination cities, tonnage,
top customers, sales-office breakdowns, and month-by-month filtering — all in
one self-contained file you can open in a browser, no server required.

## How it works

`generate_map.py` reads one or more `.xlsx` shipment exports, normalizes city
names and postal codes, groups shipments into routes, fetches real road paths
from the public [OSRM](http://project-osrm.org/) routing API (falling back to
straight lines if OSRM is unreachable, and caching results in `osrm_cache.json`
so repeat runs don't re-fetch), and writes everything into
`logistics_network_map.html`.

Required columns in the input file:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cityName` / `zipcode` | Origin city and postal code |
| `to_cityName` / `to_zipcode` | Destination city and postal code |
| `waga` | Shipment weight, in kg |
| `załadunek` | Warehouse / loading point label |

Optional columns the script picks up if present: `NrSekcji = nr trasy` (route
number), `NrZlecenia` (order number, used for counts), `TripDistance`,
`CzasZaładunku` (loading timestamp, enables month filtering), `UworzonePrzez`
(salesperson — mapped to a sales office via `BH_handlowcy.xlsx` if that file
exists alongside the script), or a direct `BiuroHandlowe` column as a
shortcut. Column names are matched flexibly (case-insensitive, common
aliases), so slightly different exports usually work without edits.

## Try it with demo data

The real shipment files used in production contain live customer data and
aren't in this repo. `demo_data/` has a small synthetic dataset with the same
column layout, plus the script that generated it (`generate_demo_data.py`),
so you can see exactly how it was built. `demo_data/logistics_network_map_demo.html`
is the pre-built output — open it directly in a browser to see the program
working without installing anything.

To regenerate it yourself:

```bash
pip install pandas numpy openpyxl
python generate_map.py demo_data/demo_data.xlsx
```

This writes `logistics_network_map.html` in the script directory. Open it in
a browser.

## Using it with your own data

Drop your `.xlsx` export(s) next to `generate_map.py` and run the script with
no arguments — it picks up every `.xlsx` file in the directory automatically
(add specific filenames as arguments to restrict it to just those files):

```bash
python generate_map.py
```

If your `UworzonePrzez` names need mapping to sales offices, add a
`BH_handlowcy.xlsx` file with `Oddział` and `Name, surname` columns next to
the script, or fix an existing export in place with:

```bash
python "napraw_biura_handlowe (1).py" your_data.xlsx
```

## Notes

- `safe_version.py` is an earlier snapshot of `generate_map.py`, kept for
  reference.
- If you see a `UnicodeEncodeError` on the console when the script finishes
  (Windows-only, non-UTF-8 terminals), the HTML output was still written
  successfully — it's just the final status print failing to render an emoji.
  Run with `set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` first if you want a clean run.
- Real shipment `.xlsx` files and the HTML generated from them are excluded
  from this repo via `.gitignore` — see `demo_data/` to evaluate the tool
  without needing them.

\# 📊 SteelQuote



A modern tool for sales professionals to calculate steel surcharges, create offers, and manage approval workflows.



\---



\## 🚀 Project Overview



\*\*SteelQuote\*\* is a web-based application designed to streamline pricing calculations for steel products. It supports sales teams in creating accurate offers quickly and efficiently.



The application works in real-time — all changes are instantly reflected in the final price without the need to refresh the page.



\---



\## ✨ Features



\### 🧮 Pricing Calculator



\* Supports multiple steel types:



  \* HRS (Hot Rolled Steel)

  \* CR (Cold Rolled Steel)

  \* HDG (Hot Dip Galvanized)

\* Automatic calculation of:



  \* Mill surcharges

  \* SSC (processing) costs

  \* Margin

  \* Transport and additional costs

\* Real-time updates



\---



\### 📄 Offer Management



\* Add items to an offer summary

\* View all positions in one place

\* Automatic total value calculation

\* Edit, duplicate, and delete entries



\---



\### 📑 PDF Export



\* Generate offers in PDF format

\* Ready to send to clients or supervisors



\---



\### 🔐 Authentication System



\* Login screen connected to a database

\* User management support

\* Planned features:



  \* “Forgot password” functionality

  \* Email server integration for password reset



\---



\### 👨‍💼 Approval Workflow



\* Send offers to a supervisor for validation

\* Approval required before sending to client

\* Structured sales process



\---



\### 🎨 UI/UX



\* Modern, clean interface

\* Light / Dark mode

\* Responsive design



\---



\## 🛠️ Tech Stack



\* HTML5

\* CSS3 (custom design system)

\* JavaScript (vanilla)



\*\*Planned / Optional:\*\*



\* Backend (e.g., Node.js / PHP / Python)

\* Database (e.g., PostgreSQL / MySQL)

\* Email integration (SMTP)




\---



\## ⚙️ Getting Started



1\. Clone the repository:



```bash

git clone https://github.com/your-repo/steel-calculator.git

```



2\. Open the app:



```bash

index.html

```



3\. Done ✅



\*(Currently runs as a frontend application — backend required for full authentication and workflow features.)\*



\---



\## 🔮 Roadmap



\* \[ ] Backend API integration

\* \[ ] User roles and permissions

\* \[ ] Full approval workflow system

\* \[ ] Complete PDF export functionality

\* \[ ] Email integration (SMTP)

\* \[ ] Offer history

\* \[ ] Sales dashboard



\---







\## 📄 License



This project is licensed under the MIT License.



\---



\## 👤 Author



Created as a tool to support sales teams in the steel industry.

## Getting Started

First, run the development server:

```bash
npm run dev
# or
yarn dev
# or
pnpm dev
# or
bun dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) with your browser to see the result.

You can start editing the page by modifying `app/page.tsx`. The page auto-updates as you edit the file.

This project uses [`next/font`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/optimizing/fonts) to automatically optimize and load [Geist](https://vercel.com/font), a new font family for Vercel.

## Learn More

- [Next.js Documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs) - learn about Next.js features and API.
- [Learn Next.js](https://nextjs.org/learn) - an interactive Next.js tutorial.

input.content:
# SteelQuote

A web app for steel sales teams: calculate pricing (mill surcharges, processing
costs, margin, transport) for HRS, CR, and HDG steel in real time, save the
result as an offer, and export it to PDF for a client.

![HRS pricing defaults](screenshot_hrs_defaults.png)
![CR pricing defaults](screenshot_cr_defaults.png)
![HDG pricing defaults](screenshot_hdg_defaults.png)

This repo has two implementations of the same idea, built at different points:

- **`finance_calculator/`** — the current version. Next.js 14 + plain
  PostgreSQL (`pg`) + JWT auth (`jose`, `bcryptjs`) + `jspdf` for PDF export.
  Lighter dependency footprint, custom auth.
- **`finance_calculator_deployed/nextjs_space/`** — an alternate build using
  Prisma + NextAuth for auth/sessions, with S3/Azure Blob storage wired in.
  Heavier, more "batteries-included" scaffold.

There's also a standalone prototype at the repo root (`index.html`,
`steel_calculator_standalone.html`) — a single-file version of the calculator
with no backend, useful for a quick look without installing anything.

## `finance_calculator/`

**Stack:** Next.js 14 (App Router), PostgreSQL, JWT sessions, jsPDF.

**Features:**
- Login backed by Postgres, passwords hashed with bcrypt, session as an
  httpOnly JWT cookie (24h expiry)
- Calculator page for HRS / CR / HDG pricing with live totals
- Offers: create, list, duplicate, delete, edit — stored per-user in Postgres
  as JSONB, with client info (name, company, NIP, address, contact) attached
- PDF export of an offer via jsPDF + jspdf-autotable

**Setup:**

```bash
cd finance_calculator
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # fill in DATABASE_URL and JWT_SECRET
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/001_create_users_table.sql
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/002_create_offers_table.sql
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/003_add_client_info_to_offers.sql
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). There's no signup route
yet — create a user manually, hashing the password with bcrypt:


# SteelQuote

A web app for steel sales teams: calculate pricing (mill surcharges, processing
costs, margin, transport) for HRS, CR, and HDG steel in real time, save the
result as an offer, and export it to PDF for a client.

![HRS pricing defaults](screenshot_hrs_defaults.png)
![CR pricing defaults](screenshot_cr_defaults.png)
![HDG pricing defaults](screenshot_hdg_defaults.png)

This repo has two implementations of the same idea, built at different points:

- **`finance_calculator/`** — the current version. Next.js 14 + plain
  PostgreSQL (`pg`) + JWT auth (`jose`, `bcryptjs`) + `jspdf` for PDF export.
  Lighter dependency footprint, custom auth.
- **`finance_calculator_deployed/nextjs_space/`** — an alternate build using
  Prisma + NextAuth for auth/sessions, with S3/Azure Blob storage wired in.
  Heavier, more "batteries-included" scaffold.

There's also a standalone prototype at the repo root (`index.html`,
`steel_calculator_standalone.html`) — a single-file version of the calculator
with no backend, useful for a quick look without installing anything.

## `finance_calculator/`

**Stack:** Next.js 14 (App Router), PostgreSQL, JWT sessions, jsPDF.

**Features:**
- Login backed by Postgres, passwords hashed with bcrypt, session as an
  httpOnly JWT cookie (24h expiry)
- Calculator page for HRS / CR / HDG pricing with live totals
- Offers: create, list, duplicate, delete, edit — stored per-user in Postgres
  as JSONB, with client info (name, company, NIP, address, contact) attached
- PDF export of an offer via jsPDF + jspdf-autotable

**Setup:**

```bash
cd finance_calculator
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # fill in DATABASE_URL and JWT_SECRET
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/001_create_users_table.sql
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/002_create_offers_table.sql
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/003_add_client_info_to_offers.sql
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). There's no signup route
yet — create a user manually, hashing the password with bcrypt:

```bash
node -e "console.log(require('bcryptjs').hashSync('yourpassword', 10))"
```

```sql

```

**Stack:** Next.js, Prisma, NextAuth, PostgreSQL, AWS S3 / Azure Blob storage.

**Setup:**

```bash

cp .env.example .env   # fill in DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, ABACUSAI_API_KEY

yarn dev
```

generation service used by `app/api/generate-pdf` — the plain

kampanie miesięczne BHP,

1. Daily login (codzienne logowanie)
Każdy pracownik może raz dziennie zdobyć punkty za samo zalogowanie się do aplikacji.

zapisywać historię logowań (data, godzina),
wspierać streak (ciągłej serii dni zalogowania – w przyszłości).
Konfiguracja:

liczba punktów za daily login powinna być konfigurowalna przez administratora (np. domyślnie 5–10 pkt).

Każdego dnia pracownik powinien mieć do wykonania zestaw np. 5 pytań BHP.
Pytania są losowane z puli pytań BHP:
pytania jednokrotnego wyboru,

Za ukończenie całego dziennego zestawu:
przyznawane są punkty (konfigurowalna liczba),

dodawania/edycji/archiwizacji pytań,
definiowania zestawów dziennych (lub logiki losowania),

Flow:
Pracownik widzi listę misji przypisanych na dany dzień/tydzień.
Gdy realnie wykona misję, klika „Wykonano”.
Status misji zmienia się na: oczekuje na zatwierdzenie.
Brygadzista w swoim panelu widzi listę zgłoszonych misji z pracownikami.
Brygadzista:
zatwierdza (approve) – pracownik otrzymuje punkty,
odrzuca (reject) – pracownik nie otrzymuje punktów (opcjonalnie komentarz).
W bazie zapisywana jest informacja: kto, kiedy zatwierdził/odrzucił misję.

Co miesiąc może być uruchomiona kampania BHP z zadaniem specjalnym, np.:
nagranie krótkiego filmu o właściwym zachowaniu podczas wypadku,
przygotowanie plakatu, opisu, prezentacji, itp.

ma nazwę, opis, okres trwania (start – koniec),

zapisuje zgłoszenia w kampanii,

Każdego dnia przed zmianą brygadzista prowadzi pre‑shift (krótka 5‑minutowa odprawa).
Podczas pre‑shiftu:
brygadzista widzi listę swoich pracowników na danej zmianie,

input.content:
# AMSafety

A gamified PWA that turns warehouse health & safety (BHP) into something
workers actually want to engage with: daily-login streaks, a points/rank
system, daily safety quizzes, leader-assigned missions, and a full
worker → team leader → manager hierarchy for oversight and approvals.

Originally built for a production warehouse environment, using employees'
existing employee IDs rather than a signup flow.

## Roles & login

Login is `employee_id` + PIN (bcrypt-hashed), not email/password — the app is
meant to be used from a phone or shared terminal on the floor. Three roles:

- **worker** — daily login, BHP quiz, missions, avatar/points, pre-shift
  check-in, news feed
- **leader** (brygadzista) — everything a worker has, plus: approve/assign
  missions, run pre-shift briefings and rate participants, manage their team,
  log violations, message their manager
- **manager** (kierownik) — oversight across leaders/teams, analytics
  dashboards, bonus points and "good practice" request approval
- **admin** — user management, question bank, news, monthly quiz config,
  certifications, system config, emergency/monthly reset tools

## Core features

- **Gamification** — points, ranks/titles with helmet-color progression,
  avatars, a monthly quiz with its own ranking and campaign items
- **BHP quiz** — a short daily quiz drawn from a question bank, plus a
  separate monthly quiz
- **Missions** — leader-created tasks workers complete for points
- **Pre-shift flow** — start/complete a shift, leader ratings, shift
  membership
- **Violations & certifications** — track safety violations and worker
  certifications, with point awards tied to certification completion
- **Bonus points / good practice requests** — workers or leaders can request
  discretionary point awards for manager approval
- **News feed** with read tracking
- **Push notifications** (Web Push / VAPID) — e.g. quiz reminders
- **Admin analytics** — activity, per-leader and per-manager breakdowns,
  a "Top 5" leaderboard view
- **File uploads** (avatars etc.) via S3-compatible storage with presigned
  URLs

## Stack

Next.js (App Router), Prisma + PostgreSQL, NextAuth-style JWT/cookie session
handling in `lib/auth.ts`, Tailwind CSS, `web-push` for notifications,
AWS S3 for file storage, deployed as an installable PWA (manifest + service
worker in `public/`).

## Setup

```bash
npm install   # or yarn
cp .env.example .env   # fill in DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, AWS_*, VAPID_*, CRON_SECRET
npx prisma migrate deploy
npx prisma db seed     # runs scripts/safe-seed.ts, which sanity-checks
                        # scripts/seed.ts for delete/deleteMany calls before
                        # running it, then seeds placeholder users/data
                        # (admin, leader, manager, a handful of workers —
                        # none of it real)
npm run dev
```

VAPID keys for push notifications can be generated with:

```bash
npx web-push generate-vapid-keys
```

## Notes

- Real employee data, generated safety/employee reports, and local build
  artifacts are excluded from this repo via `.gitignore` — see
  `scripts/seed.ts` for placeholder accounts to log in with locally
  (e.g. `EMP001` / PIN `5678`).
- `AWS_PROFILE` is used with the default AWS SDK credential chain rather than
  a hardcoded access key — see `lib/aws-config.ts`.

   ouitput ma być w wodzie aplikacja to A gamified PWA that turns warehouse health & safety (BHP)
   into something workers actually want to engage with: daily-login streaks, a points/rank system,
   daily safety quizzes, leader-assigned missions, and a full worker → team leader → manager
   hierarchy for oversight and approvals.

   Originally built for a production warehouse environment, using employees' existing employee IDs
   rather than a signup flow.

   Roles & login
   Login is employee_id + PIN (bcrypt-hashed), not email/password — the app is meant to be used from
   a phone or shared terminal on the floor. Three roles:

   worker — daily login, BHP quiz, missions, avatar/points, pre-shift check-in, news feed
   leader (brygadzista) — everything a worker has, plus: approve/assign missions, run pre-shift
   briefings and rate participants, manage their team, log violations, message their manager
   manager (kierownik) — oversight across leaders/teams, analytics dashboards, bonus points and "good
   practice" request approval
   admin — user management, question bank, news, monthly quiz config, certifications, system config,
   emergency/monthly reset tools
   Core features
   Gamification — points, ranks/titles with helmet-color progression, avatars, a monthly quiz with
   its own ranking and campaign items
   BHP quiz — a short daily quiz drawn from a question bank, plus a separate monthly quiz
   Missions — leader-created tasks workers complete for points
   Pre-shift flow — start/complete a shift, leader ratings, shift membership
   Violations & certifications — track safety violations and worker certifications, with point awards
   tied to certification completion
   Bonus points / good practice requests — workers or leaders can request discretionary point awards
   for manager approval
   News feed with read tracking
   Push notifications (Web Push / VAPID) — e.g. quiz reminders
   Admin analytics — activity, per-leader and per-manager breakdowns, a "Top 5" leaderboard view
   File uploads (avatars etc.) via S3-compatible storage with presigned URLs
   Stack
   Next.js (App Router), Prisma + PostgreSQL, NextAuth-style JWT/cookie session handling in
   lib/auth.ts, Tailwind CSS, web-push for notifications, AWS S3 for file storage, deployed as an
   installable PWA (manifest + service worker in public/).

   Setup
   npm install   # or yarn
   cp .env.example .env   # fill in DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, AWS_*, VAPID_*, CRON_SECRET
   npx prisma migrate deploy
   npx prisma db seed     # runs scripts/safe-seed.ts, which sanity-checks
                           # scripts/seed.ts for delete/deleteMany calls before
                           # running it, then seeds placeholder users/data
                           # (admin, leader, manager, a handful of workers —
                           # none of it real)
   npm run dev
   VAPID keys for push notifications can be generated with:

   npx web-push generate-vapid-keys
   Notes
   Real employee data, generated safety/employee reports, and local build artifacts are excluded from
   this repo via .gitignore — see scripts/seed.ts for placeholder accounts to log in with locally
   (e.g. EMP001 / PIN 5678).
   AWS_PROFILE is used with the default AWS SDK credential chain rather than a hardcoded access key —

644	  user        User      @relation("Top5Achiever", fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
645	  year        Int       // Rok
646	  month       Int       // Miesiąc (1-12)
647	  rank        Int       // Pozycja (1-5)
648	  points      Int       // Punkty w danym miesiącu
649	  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
650	
651	  @@unique([userId, year, month])
652	  @@map("top5_achievements")
653	}
654	
655	// Status wniosku o punkty dodatkowe
656	enum BonusRequestStatus {
657	  pending     // Oczekuje na decyzję kierownika
658	  approved    // Zatwierdzony - punkty przyznane
659	  rejected    // Odrzucony
660	}
661	
662	// Wnioski o punkty dodatkowe od brygadzistów do kierowników
663	model BonusPointsRequest {
664	  id              String              @id @default(uuid())
665	  leaderId        String              @map("leader_id")
666	  leader          User                @relation("BonusRequestLeader", fields: [leaderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
667	  workerId        String              @map("worker_id")
668	  worker          User                @relation("BonusRequestWorker", fields: [workerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
669	  managerId       String              @map("manager_id")
670	  manager         User                @relation("BonusRequestManager", fields: [managerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
671	  points          Int                 // Ilość punktów (+/-)
672	  topic           String              // Temat
673	  description     String?             // Opis (opcjonalny)
674	  status          BonusRequestStatus  @default(pending)
675	  rejectionReason String?             @map("rejection_reason")
676	  processedAt     DateTime?           @map("processed_at")
677	  createdAt       DateTime            @default(now()) @map("created_at")
678	
679	  @@map("bonus_points_requests")
680	}
681	
682	// Good practice requests - workers submit, leaders approve
683	model GoodPracticeRequest {
684	  id              String              @id @default(uuid())
685	  workerId        String              @map("worker_id")
686	  worker          User                @relation("GoodPracticeWorker", fields: [workerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
687	  leaderId        String              @map("leader_id")
688	  leader          User                @relation("GoodPracticeLeader", fields: [leaderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
689	  points          Int                 // Ilość punktów
690	  topicId         String              @map("topic_id")  // ID tematu z listy
691	  topic           String              // Nazwa tematu
692	  description     String?             // Opis (opcjonalny)
693	  status          BonusRequestStatus  @default(pending)
694	  rejectionReason String?             @map("rejection_reason")
695	  processedAt     DateTime?           @map("processed_at")
696	  createdAt       DateTime            @default(now()) @map("created_at")
697	
698	  @@map("good_practice_requests")
699	}
700	
701	// Push notification subscriptions
702	model PushSubscription {
703	  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
704	  userId      String   @map("user_id")
705	  user        User     @relation("PushSubscriptions", fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
706	  endpoint    String   @unique
707	  p256dh      String   // Public key
708	  auth        String   // Auth secret
709	  createdAt   DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
710	  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
711	
712	  @@map("push_subscriptions")
713	}
714	
715	// Częstotliwość przyznawania punktów za uprawnienia
716	enum CertificationPointsFrequency {
717	  daily     // Codziennie
718	  weekly    // Co tydzień
719	  monthly   // Co miesiąc
720	}
721	
722	// Typy uprawnień (np. suwnicowy, wózek widłowy)
723	model Certification {
724	  id                String                       @id @default(uuid())
725	  name              String                       @unique  // np. "Suwnicowy", "Wózek widłowy"
726	  description       String?
727	  points            Int                          @default(0)  // Punkty za posiadanie
728	  pointsFrequency   CertificationPointsFrequency @default(monthly) @map("points_frequency")
729	  isActive          Boolean                      @default(true) @map("is_active")
730	  createdAt         DateTime                     @default(now()) @map("created_at")
731	  updatedAt         DateTime                     @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
732	  
733	  userCertifications UserCertification[]
734	
735	  @@map("certifications")
736	}
737	
738	// Przypisanie uprawnienia do pracownika
739	model UserCertification {
740	  id                String        @id @default(uuid())
741	  userId            String        @map("user_id")
742	  user              User          @relation("CertificationHolder", fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
743	  certificationId   String        @map("certification_id")
744	  certification     Certification @relation(fields: [certificationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
745	  grantedAt         DateTime      @default(now()) @map("granted_at")
746	  expiresAt         DateTime?     @map("expires_at")  // Opcjonalna data wygaśnięcia
747	  lastPointsAwarded DateTime?     @map("last_points_awarded")  // Ostatnie przyznanie punktów
748	  isActive          Boolean       @default(true) @map("is_active")
749	
750	  @@unique([userId, certificationId])
751	  @@map("user_certifications")
752	}
753	
754	// Status zadania od kierownika
755	enum ManagerTaskStatus {
756	  pending     // Oczekuje na rozpoczęcie
757	  in_progress // W trakcie realizacji
758	  completed   // Zakończone przez brygadzistę
759	  approved    // Zatwierdzone przez kierownika
760	  rejected    // Odrzucone przez kierownika
761	}
762	
763	// Zadania od kierownika dla brygadzistów
764	model ManagerTask {
765	  id              String              @id @default(uuid())
766	  managerId       String              @map("manager_id")
767	  manager         User                @relation("ManagerTaskCreator", fields: [managerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
768	  leaderId        String              @map("leader_id")
769	  leader          User                @relation("ManagerTaskLeader", fields: [leaderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
770	  workerId        String?             @map("worker_id") // Opcjonalnie przypisany pracownik
771	  worker          User?               @relation("ManagerTaskWorker", fields: [workerId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
772	  title           String              // Tytuł zadania
773	  description     String?             // Opis (opcjonalny)
774	  points          Int                 @default(0) // Punkty za wykonanie (dla brygadzisty)
775	  workerPoints    Int                 @default(4) @map("worker_points") // Punkty dla pracownika (domyślnie 4)
776	  status          ManagerTaskStatus   @default(pending)
777	  startedAt       DateTime?           @map("started_at")
778	  completedAt     DateTime?           @map("completed_at") // Kiedy brygadzista/pracownik oznaczył jako zakończone
779	  processedAt     DateTime?           @map("processed_at") // Kiedy kierownik zatwierdził/odrzucił
780	  rejectionReason String?             @map("rejection_reason")
781	  assignDeadline  DateTime?           @map("assign_deadline") // Do kiedy można przypisać pracownika (5 min od startu)
782	  createdAt       DateTime            @default(now()) @map("created_at")
783	
784	  @@map("manager_tasks")
785	}
